algorithm: 1. Recompute spec waves via ADR-046-validation-and-delivery §3.1's rule: wave(spec) = 0 if dependsOn is empty (folds every zero-dependency spec, e.g. decision-register and current-code-migration-map, into ADR046-W0 as rank-floor members), else 1 + max(wave(dep) for dep in dependsOn); the four declared closing specs (security-and-threat-model, streamline, reset-and-cutover, feasibility-and-spikes) plus this spec (validation-and-delivery) always resolve to ADR046-W7 by declaration regardless of computed depth, since ADR-046-validation-and-delivery §3.1 states wave placement is latest-safe, not earliest-possible.
2. Assign every work item's wave from its own specId's computed wave (implements-spec edge); a work item never carries an independently computed wave.

3. Recompute work-item-depends-on edges by re-running the deterministic dependencyOwner token scan (exact-match against the current full workItemId set, plus 'PREFIX-NNN through PREFIX-MMM' inclusive range expansion) with the same-spec/-wave cycle-breaking tie-break: a raw mutual reference pair keeps only the edge from the lexicographically smaller workItemId to the larger one, downgrading the reverse reference to peerReferences.

4. Recompute rank via Kahn's algorithm (longest path) over the union of spec-depends-on, implements-spec, and work-item-depends-on edges, using ascending node-id string order as the deterministic tie-break at every step so the output is byte-identical for identical input.

5. Re-run the destination-field exact-path-substring scan across every work item (backtick-quoted `packages/...`, `nixos-modules/...`, `docs/...` paths with a file extension, excluding brace-glob and bare-directory tokens) to detect newly shared files across different specId claimants; any new same-wave claimant cluster is added to sharedPrepBarriers and any cross-wave cluster to crossWaveContentions, in the same commit that discovers it, per ADR-046-validation-and-delivery §6.2 item 4.
